## Week 1, September 2nd

-   **Topics:** Course overview, logistics, introduction to R

-   **Lecture**: [Week 1 - Introduction](/slides/week_01_intro.html)

-   **Required Readings**

    -   Grimmer, Justin, Margaret E. Roberts, and Brandon M. Stewart. Text as data: A new framework for machine learning and the social sciences. Princeton University Press, 2022 - Chapter 2.

-   And one of the three below:

    -   Political Science Perspective: [Wilkerson, J. and Casas, A. (2017). Large-Scale Computerized Text Analysis in Political Science: Opportunities and Challenges. Annual Review of Political Science, 20, 529:544.](https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/abs/10.1146/annurev-polisci-052615-025542?journalCode=polisci)

    -   Economics Perspective: [Gentzkow, Matthew, Bryan Kelly, and Matt Taddy. "Text as data." Journal of Economic Literature 57, no. 3 (2019): 535-574.](https://web.stanford.edu/~gentzkow/research/text-as-data.pdf)

    -   Sociology Perspective: [Macanovic, A., 2022. Text mining for social science–The state and the future of computational text analysis in sociology. Social Science Research, 108, p.102784.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0049089X22000904)
